main_body: A flat wall face (dark blue-grey panel wall with an orange rail, rivets, two copper shelves/bars, a vent grille and a dark baseboard), drawn straight from the front
top_band: none: the column starts with a 1-row light outline, then dark blue-grey rows 2-4, then an orange rail row 5 and brown rows 6-20 that read as the wall face; no horizontal top surface
evidence: Terrain kind wall face tile: the whole drawing is a vertical wall surface seen face-on. The orange strip at row 5-6 is a trim rail, not a top surface. The panels, shelves, and vent are painted flat on the face with no inset. For a wall-face terrain tile this front view is the expected construction, but by the 3/4 contract there is no top band and no eave shadow, so it reads as a front elevation. Strict reading: fail.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 14 distinct colours versus 68 and 33 in the references, and 9 colours per tile versus 26 and 13. Flat-fill coverage is 30% against 0% in both references. The panels are large areas of one blue-grey with only a few rivet dots and thin lines; there is no grain, plaster speckle or per-block shading. The outlines are tinted dark blue (0% neutral), which is fine, but the material ramps have only about 3 steps (dark navy, mid blue-grey, light edge) against 5-6 in the references. It looks flatter and thinner than the reference walls.
